In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hepcidin gene is not expressed in mouse liver, and that the hepcidine gene is not expressed at all in mice.
hepcidin peptides can now be measured in serum and urine, and that this is an essential step forward for the study of hepcidins in experimental mouse models.
the hepcidin peptides in serum are a good indicator of the hepcidins in liver and spleen, but that the hepcids in urine are not a good indicator for the hepcid levels in the liver or spleen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hepcidin peptides in mouse serum and/or urine can be measured and used as an indicator for the regulation of the hepcidin gene and its role in iron homeostatic processes.
the mouse is a valuable animal model to study hepcidin, but that hepcidin peptide levels are a better marker than hepcidin gene expression to unravel the biology of this peptide.
the hepcidin peptide responses in experimental mice agree with the known hepcidin biology and their measurement can be implemented in experimental mice to provide novel insights.

the measurement of hepcidins in mouse models can be implemented in experimental studies to provide novel insights into the regulation of iron metabolism.
